minor_characters.name: Ewing Klipspringer
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A perpetually visiting 'boarder' at Gatsby’s who plays piano during Daisy’s visit (Ch 005) and later telephones only to ask for his tennis shoes back (Ch 009).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His functions (background music, a comic postmortem phone call) can be folded into anonymous servants/guests without changing any plot turn or theme the synopsis requires.

minor_characters.name: Catherine
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Myrtle Wilson’s sister at the Manhattan apartment gathering who gossips and later lies to the coroner (Ch 002, Ch 009).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her chatter and later denial add color but no consequence to the affair, the fatal accident, or the fallout described in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Mr. McKee (Chester McKee)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A fussy photographer at the Manhattan apartment party (Ch 002).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is pure background satire at Myrtle’s party and never affects the affair, the death, or Gatsby’s arc.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. McKee (Lucille McKee)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chester’s shrill wife at the Manhattan apartment party (Ch 002).
minor_characters.reason_removable: She amplifies the scene’s tawdriness but has no bearing on any later event.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Sloane
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A haughty rider who briefly visits Gatsby’s and pointedly excludes him from dinner (Ch 006).
minor_characters.reason_removable: This snub reiterates East Egg snobbery already conveyed elsewhere without shifting any outcome.

minor_characters.name: Lucille
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A named party guest in twin scenes of Gatsby’s parties who repeats rumors and a dress anecdote (Ch 003).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her gossip is duplicative of the general rumor-swirl that the synopsis already captures.

minor_characters.name: Chester Becker (representative of the guest‑list names)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Appears only in Nick’s long roster of partygoers (Ch 004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He exists solely in a catalog that can be trimmed without cost to story or theme.

minor_characters.name: Doctor Webster Civet
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named in the party guest‑list (Ch 004) and later invoked as 'Doc Civet' at a drunken table (Ch 006).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A marginal namecheck whose presence never influences any scene that matters to the main arc.

minor_characters.name: Michaelis
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The coffee‑stall owner who narrates George Wilson’s night of grief (Ch 007–008).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Nick can summarize Wilson’s despair and movements without inserting Michaelis as a character and nothing in the synopsis depends on him.

minor_characters.name: ‘Blocks’ Biloxi
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A comic wedding anecdote figure raised during the Plaza confrontation (Ch 007).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The anecdote is digressive comedy that neither alters Daisy’s wavering nor Tom and Gatsby’s showdown.

minor_characters.name: Rosy Rosenthal
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A murdered gambler in Wolfshiem’s reminiscence at lunch (Ch 004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He serves only to thicken Wolfshiem’s aura; excising him leaves Wolfshiem’s role in Gatsby’s 'drugstore' business intact.

minor_characters.name: Motorcycle policeman
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Pulls Gatsby over and is waved off by a 'Christmas card' (Ch 004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: This roadside cameo is a throwaway hint of Gatsby’s pull and can be dropped without changing any later beat.

minor_characters.name: Ferdie (Daisy’s chauffeur)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly named when Daisy arrives at Nick’s cottage for tea (Ch 005).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Swapping him for an unnamed driver has zero effect on the reunion or its consequences.

subplots.name: Nick’s New York work life and Jersey City fling
subplots.reason_removable: His office routine and brief romance are self‑contained diversions that don’t touch the Gatsby–Daisy–Tom triangle or the novel’s outcome.

subplots.name: Jordan Baker’s golf scandal and the 'bad drivers' mini‑essay
subplots.reason_removable: Her alleged cheating and driving maxim are side character notes; the synopsis needs only that Nick later breaks with Jordan.

subplots.name: Owl Eyes’s library discovery and the car‑in‑the‑ditch gag
subplots.reason_removable: You can let Owl Eyes appear unnamed or newly named at the funeral without earlier comic set‑pieces.

subplots.name: Wolfshiem’s Rosy Rosenthal murder reminiscence
subplots.reason_removable: The anecdote is flavor; Wolfshiem’s essential functions (shadowy 'fixer,' Gatsby’s business partner) survive without it.

subplots.name: Gatsby’s 'Christmas card' from the police commissioner
subplots.reason_removable: It’s a one‑off wink at his influence that can be cut without weakening the criminal-connection thread already carried by Wolfshiem.

subplots.name: Mr. Sloane’s perfunctory invitation and snub
subplots.reason_removable: This dinner fake‑out restates East Egg hauteur already visible at the Plaza and in Tom’s behavior.

subplots.name: Catherine’s Catholic lie and Monte Carlo tangent
subplots.reason_removable: Her claims are colorful but unnecessary to establishing Tom’s affair and the apartment melee that ends with Myrtle’s broken nose.

subplots.name: Klipspringer’s posthumous 'tennis shoes' phone call
subplots.reason_removable: Wolfsheim’s refusal and the vanishing party crowd already make the funeral’s emptiness clear.

subplots.name: Biloxi-at-the-wedding comic detour during the Plaza scene
subplots.reason_removable: The story stalls the confrontation and adds no new leverage to Daisy’s waver or Tom’s counterattack.

digressions.topic: Nick’s full page(s) of rostered party names from his old timetable
digressions.reason_removable: This taxonomic guest list is pure social color; trimming it won’t affect any scene the synopsis depends on.

digressions.topic: Baroque inventory of party logistics (oranges machine, caterers’ canvas, instrument roll‑call)
digressions.reason_removable: The lavish cataloguing can be compressed to 'huge parties every weekend' without loss of plot or theme.

digressions.topic: Carraway genealogy and great‑uncle portrait (Dukes of Buccleuch, Civil War substitute, hardware business)
digressions.reason_removable: It’s background pedigree that exceeds what’s needed for 'Midwesterner Nick moves East' in the synopsis.

digressions.topic: The 'butler’s nose' anecdote and sundry small‑talk curlicues at the Buchanans’
digressions.reason_removable: These comic asides don’t move the lunch‑to‑Plaza chain of events.
You can keep Nick’s 'East like a night scene by El Greco' and return‑home resolution while paring this nostalgic excursus.
